title: Rights and responsibilities at work
keyIdea: In the UK the law sets a minimum hourly rate that depends on your age. From 1 April 2026 it is £12.71 at 21 and over (the National Living Wage), £10.85 at 18 to 20, and £8.00 under 18 or as an apprentice under 19 or in the first year. Every worker has the right to an itemised payslip, a written statement of their main terms from day one, paid holiday and rest breaks: 20 minutes for a shift over 6 hours at 18 and over, or 30 minutes over 4½ hours if under 18. Deductions such as a uniform charge cannot take your pay below the minimum. Your side is to be reliable, on time and to follow safety training. If something is wrong, check your payslip and contract, talk to your manager, raise a written grievance, then get free advice from Acas or report unpaid minimum wage to HMRC.
familyTip: Look at a real or sample payslip together. Find the hours, the hourly rate, the gross pay and each deduction, and check the rate against the gov.uk minimum wage page for the worker's age.

visual.caption: Is this pay legal from 1 April 2026? Drag each job to a box, or tap the job and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort pay offers by age, find the error on three payslips, set legal rest breaks, sort rights from duties and plan a fix.

kid: When you start a job in the UK, the law sets the lowest hourly pay you can get. It depends on your age. From 1 April 2026 it is £12.71 an hour at 21 and over, £10.85 at 18 to 20, and £8.00 if you are under 18 or a new apprentice. The rates go up each April.

Your employer must give you a payslip every payday. Check three things. Do the hours match your rota? Is the rate at least the minimum for your age? Does any deduction, such as a charge for your uniform, take you below the minimum? If it does, that is not allowed.

You also get rest breaks. At 18 or over, a shift of more than 6 hours gives you a 20-minute break. Under 18, more than 4½ hours gives you 30 minutes. You get paid holiday and a written statement of your job terms from your first day.

Rights come with responsibilities. Turn up on time, follow the safety training and tell your manager early if you are ill. If your pay or breaks are wrong, check your payslip, then talk to your manager. If that fails, write a formal complaint called a grievance. Acas gives free advice, and HMRC can make an employer pay what you are owed.
adult: Ages 16 to 18. The PSHE Association programme of study for key stage 5 covers rights and responsibilities at work, including pay, contracts and where to get help. The rates here come from the National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Regulations 2026, in force from 1 April 2026: £12.71 (21+), £10.85 (18 to 20), £8.00 (16 to 17) and £8.00 (apprentices under 19 or in the first year).

Under the Working Time Regulations 1998, adult workers get a 20-minute uninterrupted break when the working day is longer than 6 hours. Young workers above school-leaving age but under 18 get 30 minutes when it is longer than 4.5 hours. Breaks need not be paid. Statutory holiday is 5.6 weeks a year, pro rata for part-time. Employees and workers have the right to an itemised payslip and a written statement of particulars from day one. Deductions for items such as a required uniform count against minimum wage pay.

Common mistakes: thinking under-18s have no minimum wage; using last year's rate after 1 April; thinking a deduction is fine because the worker signed for it. Others apply the under-18 break rule to an 18-year-old, or think a break is owed on any adult shift. Some treat a payslip as a favour. Some walk out or post online before they raise a written grievance. In the lab each slip gets feedback that names it.

practice.prompt: Jo is 17. What is the lowest legal hourly rate for her from 1 April 2026?
practice.hint: Under 18 has its own rate. It is the same as the apprentice rate.
practice.explain: From 1 April 2026 the minimum for 16 and 17 year olds is £8.00 an hour.

practice.prompt: Sam is 19 and works {h} hours at the 18 to 20 minimum, 1085 pence an hour (£10.85). What is his gross pay in pence?
practice.hint: Gross pay in pence is hours × 1085: {h} × 1085.
practice.explain: {h} × 1085 = {=h*1085} pence before any tax or deductions. 100 pence make £1.

practice.prompt: Priya is 22 and is paid 1250 pence an hour for {h} hours. The minimum is 1271 pence. How many pence short is she?
practice.hint: She is 21 pence short for every hour. Multiply 21 by {h}.
practice.explain: 1271 − 1250 = 21 pence an hour. × {h} hours = {=h*21} pence short.

practice.prompt: Ana is 17 and works a 5-hour shift. What break is she owed by law?
practice.hint: Under 18 the limit is 4½ hours, not 6.
practice.explain: Young workers under 18 get a 30-minute break when they work more than 4½ hours. 5 hours is more.

practice.prompt: Kit's boss takes £30 for his uniform, which drops his pay below the minimum wage. Is that allowed?
choices: Yes, the uniform is his cost
Yes, if he signed for it
practice.hint: Work out his pay per hour after the deduction.
practice.explain: A deduction for a uniform you must wear counts against minimum wage pay, so it cannot take you below the minimum, even if you signed.

pool.prompt: Dev is 20. What is the lowest legal hourly rate for him from April 2026?
pool.explain: From 1 April 2026 the 18 to 20 rate is £10.85. £12.71 starts at 21.

pool.prompt: Lucy is 18 and works 7 hours. What break is she owed?
choices: None if the shop is busy
pool.hint: At 18 she is an adult worker.
pool.explain: Adult workers get 20 minutes when the day is over 6 hours. The 30-minute rule is for under 18s.

pool.prompt: Tom is 24 and works {h} hours at 1271 pence an hour (£12.71). What is his gross pay in pence?
pool.explain: {h} × 1271 = {=h*1271} pence before any tax or deductions.

pool.prompt: Who has the right to an itemised payslip?
choices: Every employee and worker, every payday
pool.hint: Is it a legal right or a favour?
pool.explain: All employees and workers have the right to an itemised payslip on or before payday.

pool.prompt: Which of these is your responsibility at work?
choices: Following the safety training you were given
pool.hint: What does your employer expect from you?
pool.explain: You must follow safety training and work reliably. Payslips are the employer's job; the government sets the minimum wage.

pool.prompt: Your pay is still wrong after you talked to your manager. What is a good next step?
choices: Raise a formal grievance in writing
Stop going in without telling anyone
pool.hint: Put the problem on record inside work first.
pool.explain: A written grievance starts the employer's formal process. Acas can give free advice at any stage.

pool.prompt: Kit is 18 and paid 17360 pence for 16 hours, but a {d} pence uniform charge is taken off. What is his pay after the deduction, in pence?
pool.hint: Take {d} away from 17360, then compare with 16 × 1085 = 17360.
pool.explain: 17360 − {d} = {=17360-d} pence. That is below the 17360 pence minimum for 16 hours, so the deduction is not allowed.

pool.prompt: Grace is 22. In May 2026 her payslip shows £12.21 an hour. What is wrong?
choices: £12.21 was the old rate; she needs at least £12.71
pool.hint: Rates change on 1 April each year.
pool.explain: £12.21 was the 21+ rate until 31 March 2026. From 1 April 2026 it is £12.71.
